official_scope: 2009 H1N1 influenza hemagglutinin sialic acid binding site (plus protein structure/function exam)
design_notes: Expanded each locked topic into atomic concepts aligned to the three tested modes: foundational protein chemistry, hemagglutinin-specific binding, and applied modeling/visualization. Concept counts vary by topic density; foundational and binding chapters carry more nodes because they support more discrete calculations, recognition tasks, and interaction analyses. Physical model and visualization chapters are slightly leaner but still cover rubric, software, and construction skills without padding.

topics.title: Amino acid structure and side-chain chemistry

concepts.title: Amino acid backbone and functional groups
concepts.description: Identify the α-carbon, amino group, carboxyl group, and variable R-group that define each amino acid.

concepts.title: Three-letter and one-letter amino acid codes
concepts.description: Convert among amino acid names, three-letter codes, and one-letter codes for the 20 standard amino acids.

concepts.title: L-amino acid stereochemistry
concepts.description: Recognize the L configuration of α-amino acids and explain why glycine is achiral.

concepts.title: Hydrophobic side-chain recognition
concepts.description: Identify aliphatic and aromatic side chains that favor burial in protein cores and recognize their structural roles.

concepts.title: Polar uncharged side-chain recognition
concepts.description: Identify polar side chains that can donate or accept hydrogen bonds without gaining a full charge at pH 7.

concepts.title: Acidic side-chain ionization
concepts.description: Predict the deprotonated, negatively charged state of aspartate and glutamate side chains at physiological pH using pKa values.

concepts.title: Basic side-chain ionization
concepts.description: Predict the protonated, positively charged state of lysine and arginine side chains at physiological pH using pKa values.

concepts.title: Histidine protonation and pH sensitivity
concepts.description: Analyze the imidazole side chain of histidine and predict its partially protonated state near physiological pH.

concepts.title: Cysteine thiol group
concepts.description: Recognize the thiol side chain of cysteine and identify its redox sensitivity and role as a metal-binding or nucleophilic site.

concepts.title: Glycine and proline backbone effects
concepts.description: Explain how glycine increases backbone flexibility and proline restricts conformation through its cyclic side chain.

concepts.title: Aromatic side-chain properties
concepts.description: Identify aromatic side chains and interpret properties such as UV absorbance and stacking interactions.

concepts.title: Isoelectric point calculation for amino acids
concepts.description: Calculate the isoelectric point of an amino acid from its pKa values and identify the zwitterionic species.

concepts.title: Primary structure and amino acid sequence
concepts.description: Define primary structure as the linear sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

concepts.title: Peptide bond planarity and cis/trans
concepts.description: Explain the partial double-bond character of the peptide bond and the preference for trans configuration.

concepts.title: Alpha-helix structure and hydrogen bonding
concepts.description: Describe the α-helix geometry, 3.6 residues per turn, and i to i+4 backbone hydrogen bonding.

concepts.title: Beta-sheet structure and strand arrangement
concepts.description: Distinguish parallel and antiparallel β-sheets and describe hydrogen bonding between adjacent β-strands.

concepts.title: Loops, turns, and irregular secondary structure
concepts.description: Identify loop and turn regions that connect regular secondary structures and provide surface functionality.

concepts.title: Backbone dihedral angles and Ramachandran plot
concepts.description: Interpret φ and ψ backbone angles and use a Ramachandran plot to assess allowed secondary-structure conformations.

concepts.title: Tertiary structure and domain packing
concepts.description: Describe how secondary structure elements pack into a compact three-dimensional fold with a buried hydrophobic core.

concepts.title: Quaternary structure and subunit assembly
concepts.description: Describe how multiple polypeptide chains assemble into oligomeric structures and recognize homomeric vs heteromeric assemblies.

concepts.title: Hydrophobic effect in protein folding
concepts.description: Explain how exclusion of nonpolar side chains from water drives the burial of hydrophobic residues and stabilizes the folded state.

concepts.title: Hydrogen bonding in folded proteins
concepts.description: Identify hydrogen bonds involving backbone amides, carbonyls, and polar side chains that stabilize secondary and tertiary structure.

concepts.title: Electrostatic interactions and salt bridges
concepts.description: Describe how oppositely charged side chains form salt bridges and how pH changes affect electrostatic stabilization.

concepts.title: Disulfide bonds as covalent stabilizers
concepts.description: Explain how cysteine oxidation forms disulfide bonds that covalently stabilize tertiary and quaternary structure, especially in secreted proteins.

concepts.title: Denaturation and loss of native structure
concepts.description: Predict how heat, pH extremes, reducing agents, or denaturants disrupt noncovalent interactions and unfold proteins.

topics.title: Hemagglutinin structure and sialic acid receptor binding

concepts.title: Hemagglutinin trimer architecture
concepts.description: Describe the homotrimeric hemagglutinin spike and distinguish the globular head from the fibrous stalk.

concepts.title: HA1 and HA2 subunit roles
concepts.description: Identify HA1 as the receptor-binding subunit and HA2 as the fusion subunit of the hemagglutinin glycoprotein.

concepts.title: Sialic acid structure and linkage types
concepts.description: Recognize N-acetylneuraminic acid and distinguish α2-3 and α2-6 glycosidic linkages to galactose.

concepts.title: Hemagglutinin receptor binding pocket
concepts.description: Locate the receptor binding pocket in the HA1 globular head and identify its conserved structural elements.

concepts.title: 3UBE chain A residue 153–252 target region
concepts.description: Map the 2009 H1N1 hemagglutinin PDB entry 3UBE chain A residues 153–252 and identify their position in the receptor binding domain.

concepts.title: Key residues in the H1 sialic acid binding pocket
concepts.description: Identify conserved residues in the 3UBE binding site that form direct contacts with sialic acid.

concepts.title: Protein–sialic acid interaction types
concepts.description: Analyze hydrogen bonds, van der Waals contacts, and hydrophobic packing that stabilize sialic acid in the HA binding pocket.

concepts.title: H1 hemagglutinin receptor specificity
concepts.description: Explain how H1 hemagglutinin from 2009 H1N1 preferentially binds human α2-6-linked sialic acid receptors over avian α2-3-linked receptors.

concepts.title: 130-loop, 190-helix, and 220-loop roles
concepts.description: Describe how the 130-loop, 190-helix, and 220-loop shape the receptor binding site and influence receptor specificity.

concepts.title: Hemagglutinin glycosylation and receptor access
concepts.description: Explain how N-linked glycans on HA can mask antigenic sites and modulate receptor binding affinity.

concepts.title: Hemagglutinin multivalent binding and avidity
concepts.description: Explain how the trimeric HA can engage multiple sialic acid receptors and how multivalent binding contributes to overall avidity.

concepts.title: Influenza virus particle structure and genome
concepts.description: Describe the influenza virion envelope, HA and NA spikes, matrix layer, and segmented negative-sense RNA genome.

concepts.title: Hemagglutinin-mediated viral entry
concepts.description: Explain how HA binds sialic acid on host cells to initiate endocytosis and viral entry.

concepts.title: Endosomal pH-triggered membrane fusion
concepts.description: Describe how low endosomal pH triggers HA conformational change, exposing the fusion peptide and mediating viral-host membrane fusion.

concepts.title: Influenza replication and assembly
concepts.description: Summarize viral RNA replication, protein synthesis, and assembly at the host cell membrane.

concepts.title: Neuraminidase cleavage and viral release
concepts.description: Explain how neuraminidase cleaves sialic acid to release newly budded virions from infected cells.

concepts.title: Antigenic drift in hemagglutinin
concepts.description: Describe how point mutations in HA accumulate and alter antigenic sites to evade antibody recognition.

concepts.title: Antigenic shift and pandemic emergence
concepts.description: Explain how reassortment of RNA segments between influenza strains produces novel HA/NA combinations that can cause pandemics.

concepts.title: Host immune recognition of hemagglutinin
concepts.description: Describe how B cells produce antibodies against HA epitopes and how neutralizing antibodies block receptor binding.

concepts.title: Vaccine targeting of hemagglutinin
concepts.description: Explain how influenza vaccines elicit antibodies against HA and why antigenic drift requires seasonal reformulation.

concepts.title: 2009 H1N1 pandemic origin and adaptation
concepts.description: Trace the origin of the 2009 H1N1 pandemic strain and identify adaptive mutations in HA that enabled human transmission.

topics.title: Molecular visualization and chemical environment analysis

concepts.title: Jmol/JUDE interface navigation
concepts.description: Use Jmol/JUDE menus and command line to open files, rotate, zoom, and select parts of a protein structure.

concepts.title: Selecting and displaying residues
concepts.description: Select specific residues, chains, ligands, or side chains in Jmol and display them as sticks, wireframe, or spacefill.

concepts.title: Visualizing secondary structure in Jmol
concepts.description: Identify α-helices and β-strands using cartoon or ribbon representations and interpret their spatial arrangement.

concepts.title: Color-by-property representations
concepts.description: Apply color schemes based on residue type, charge, hydrophobicity, or secondary structure to visualize chemical environments.

concepts.title: Identifying hydrogen bonds in visualization
concepts.description: Display hydrogen bonds between protein side chains, backbone, and ligands to diagnose interaction networks.

concepts.title: Identifying hydrophobic contacts in protein core
concepts.description: Interpret clustering of nonpolar side chains in the protein core and around ligand surfaces using hydrophobic surface views.

concepts.title: Electrostatic potential surface visualization
concepts.description: Display electrostatic potential surfaces to identify acidic, basic, and neutral regions involved in binding or stability.

concepts.title: Protein–ligand interaction display
concepts.description: Display a sialic acid ligand in the hemagglutinin binding pocket and identify contacting residues within 4 Å.

concepts.title: Analyzing side-chain chemical environment
concepts.description: Assess whether a side chain is buried or solvent-exposed and infer its likely role from surrounding residues.

concepts.title: Measuring distances and angles in Jmol
concepts.description: Measure interatomic distances, hydrogen bond lengths, and ligand contact geometry to support structural interpretations.

concepts.title: Conservation and mutation mapping
concepts.description: Map conserved residues and known mutations onto the HA structure to interpret antigenic or binding changes.

topics.title: Physical model construction and Model Description Legend

concepts.title: α-Carbon backbone model scaling
concepts.description: Construct a physical model with an α-carbon backbone spaced at 2 cm per amino acid to represent the target chain.

concepts.title: Mapping target residues 153–252 of 3UBE chain A
concepts.description: Translate the protein sequence of 3UBE chain A residues 153–252 into a physical model with correct order and spacing.

concepts.title: Representing secondary structure in physical model
concepts.description: Use α-helix and β-sheet geometry to shape the physical backbone model according to the target structure.

concepts.title: Displaying functional side chains in physical model
concepts.description: Attach and display side chains or functional groups at specified residues to highlight binding-site chemistry or stabilizing interactions.

concepts.title: Model Description Legend requirements
concepts.description: Create a legend that explains colors, materials, and structural features shown in the physical model.

concepts.title: Pre-build scoring criteria
concepts.description: Interpret pre-build rubric categories such as backbone accuracy, secondary structure, side chain display, and legend quality.

concepts.title: Backbone accuracy and residue connectivity
concepts.description: Maintain correct residue order, connectivity, and spacing along the α-carbon backbone to maximize structural accuracy.

concepts.title: Materials and construction techniques
concepts.description: Select appropriate materials and techniques to build a stable, adjustable physical model within competition constraints.

concepts.title: Color conventions and labeling in physical model
concepts.description: Apply clear color and labeling conventions to distinguish chain, secondary structure, and key residues in the physical model.

concepts.title: Legend annotations for binding site features
concepts.description: Annotate sialic acid binding site residues, loops, and stabilizing interactions in the Model Description Legend to communicate functional features.
